outcome: Correlations between fetal limb volumes and neonatal anthropometric parameters
Relationship of TVol and AVol with neonatal measurements (birth weight, crown-heel length, arm and leg lengths, head, abdominal, mid-thigh, and mid-arm circumferences, skinfold thicknesses)
cohort: 40 medically and obstetrically uncomplicated pregnancies scheduled for elective cesarean section
finding: Fetal AVol measurements by 3D ultrasound before delivery showed significant correlations with most neonatal morphometric indices, independent of maternal characteristics and 2D biometric parameters, suggesting that AVol may be more advantageous than TVol in assessing limb soft tissue development in term fetuses.
